back: Prior $\mathcal N(0,\tau^2)$ and noise variance $\sigma^2$ give $\lambda=\sigma^2/\tau^2$; the penalty is the negative log prior.

front: L1 versus L2 on a 1-D example $\tfrac12(w-3)^2$
back: L2: $w=3/(1+\lambda)$ (shrinks, never zero). L1: $\mathrm{sign}(3)\max(3-\lambda,0)$ (exact zero once $\lambda\ge3$).

front: Which parameters usually get weight decay?
back: Weight matrices; biases and normalisation scales are normally excluded.
$\tilde a=m\odot a/(1-p)$ with $m_i\sim\mathrm{Bernoulli}(1-p)$; identity at evaluation.
$\mathbb{E}[m]=1-p$, so $\mathbb{E}[\tilde a]=a$: train and test see the same expected activation scale.
$\bar a=\bar{\tilde a}\odot m/(1-p)$ with the same mask as forward.
Forgetting $\texttt{model.eval()}$ at test time, or resampling the mask in backward.
Track validation loss, checkpoint the best epoch, stop after a patience window without improvement, restore the best checkpoint.

front: Why must validation differ from test?
back: Choosing the stopping epoch on the test set leaks it and makes the reported score optimistic.
Small zero-mean transformations give $E+\lambda\Omega$ to second order: a penalty on sensitivity to the transformation.
Training loss keeps falling while validation loss turns upward; a growing train/test gap.
Training loss itself stays high (underfitting); e.g. $\lambda=0.1$ dropped training accuracy to 0.875 in the lesson experiment.
